- .claude/commands/claude-issue-pickup.md:33-59 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The `start — restart` path is reported to allow overlapping pickup sessions to read and dispatch the same queue item because its success path lacks the AD-10 carve-out, although deepseek reports that the carve-out is present there.
  WHY: Minimax, OpenAI, and GLM describe a duplicate-session race caused by non-atomic downstream checks; deepseek disputes the missing-carve-out diagnosis and says the success path and test confirm it. The highest reported severity is MAJOR; deepseek rated its opposing report NIT.
- .claude/commands/claude-issue-pickup.md:33-41 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: If the old pickup's trigger is deleted, archiving its session is denied, and creating the replacement trigger fails twice, the carve-out can defer queue processing even though no hourly wake is scheduled.
  WHY: The pickup ends without reading the queue or arranging another attempt, leaving queued work stalled.
- tests/test_implement_issue_claude_command.py:370-371 | severity=low | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The contract test can pass by finding the carve-out phrase in the `create_trigger` failure branch without verifying that the success path enforces it.
  WHY: As written, the assertion does not detect a missing success-path guard; minimax rated this NIT.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: AD-10 — "a restart that leaves any other pickup's session unarchived creates its trigger but reads no queue in that turn; its first read is its first hourly wake, when the old wake has finished."
  expected_change_site: .claude/commands/claude-issue-pickup.md, step 1, `start` mode body — the create_trigger SUCCESS path
  confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [z-ai_glm-5_2]
  EVIDENCE: The `start` mode body (line 33) describes delete + archive + create_trigger, then falls through to step 2. The carve-out ("unless this step left another pickup's session unarchived: then do not read the queue in this turn") appears only in the create_trigger FAILURE branch (line 38). The create_trigger SUCCESS path has no equivalent gate. The Cleanup calls paragraph (line 41) states the rule declaratively but does not gate the body's success-path flow. The contract test (test_implement_issue_claude_command.py:370-372) asserts the carve-out phrase is present in the `start` section, but the phrase lives in the failure branch — the test passes without the success path enforcing the rule.
- requirement: The contract test must verify the `start` mode create_trigger SUCCESS path enforces the AD-10 carve-out (plan Tests section: "each implement-plan-claude cleanup site ... states the skip rule")
  expected_change_site: tests/test_implement_issue_claude_command.py::test_pickup_skips_a_denied_cleanup_call, `start` section assertions (lines 370-372)
  confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [z-ai_glm-5_2]
  EVIDENCE: The test slices `start = keep_one[keep_one.index("**`start`**"):keep_one.index("**`— wake.`**")]` and asserts the carve-out phrase is present. The phrase is in the create_trigger failure branch (line 38 of the pickup), so the test passes. No assertion verifies that the success path (create_trigger succeeds, archive denied) also defers the queue read. A future regression removing the success-path rule (once added) would not be caught.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

  WHY: If deleting the old trigger succeeded, archiving the old session was denied, and creating the replacement trigger failed twice, the carve-out prevents queue reading even though no trigger remains to wake the old session.

  WHY: Both pickups may read the queue while the older pickup is mid-processing; the race window is small but non-zero.
